finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-controlled POST 'feed' is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents, letting remote users make the server fetch arbitrary URLs (internal hosts, cloud metadata, file:// wrappers). Response leaks only strlen, so exploitation is blind.
finding.source: $_POST['feed'] (import.php:11-12), HTTP POST parameter, no authentication required

trace.note: session_start(); no auth check precedes the feed branch
Branch guard checks only REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed'])
$xml = file_get_contents($_POST['feed']); raw user value used as fetch URL
echo strlen($xml); only the body length is returned (blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: Authentication: none (require_admin not called on this branch). Scheme allowlist: none (http, https, file, php, ftp reachable). Host/IP allow- or denylist: none (loopback, RFC1918, 169.254.169.254 reachable). Port restriction: none. Redirect control: none; PHP http wrapper follows redirects by default, which would defeat any future URL allowlist. Method hardening beyond POST check: none.

verdict.guard_found: none. import.php:11 checks only REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' and isset($_POST['feed']); there is no require_admin() call on this branch (require_admin is defined at lines 4-9 and used only at line 18), no URL scheme, host, port, or redirect validation before file_get_contents at line 12.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled $_POST['feed'] reaches file_get_contents() unvalidated at import.php:12 with no authentication, since the branch at import.php:11 is reached before and independently of the admin check at import.php:18, and only strlen of the result is echoed at import.php:13, so the SSRF is blind but still valid.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: the 'set_webhook' POST value is passed unvalidated to curl_init and executed server-side. Requires an admin session, so lower severity; response is discarded, so exploitation is blind.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (import.php:17-19), HTTP POST parameter, reachable only after require_admin()
finding.sink: curl_init($hook) at import.php:20 followed by curl_exec($ch) at import.php:22

trace.note: require_admin() checks only that $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty; exits 403 otherwise
$ch = curl_init($hook); URL passed to libcurl unchanged
CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER set; response is not returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Authentication: require_admin() checks only non-empty $_SESSION['is_admin'], not its value; how the session is set is outside this file. Scheme/host/IP/port restrictions: none. Redirect control: CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION not set (defaults off). Protocol restriction (CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS): not set, so libcurl defaults apply and depend on libcurl version (unverified). Response: discarded.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at import.php:4-9 checks only that $_SESSION['is_admin'] is non-empty. No hostname, scheme, or IP validation exists before curl_init at import.php:20. The admin gate is what makes the source non-attacker-controlled.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (import.php:17-22), but the source $_POST['set_webhook'] is only reachable after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes, so it is controlled by an admin, not an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, which fails the source check. This holds only if $_SESSION['is_admin'] cannot be set by lower-privileged users; session assignment is not in this directory, so that is unverified. Separately, the unauthenticated $_POST['feed'] path at import.php:11-13 passes a raw value to file_get_contents with no auth, which is outside this candidate's claim and should be reviewed on its own.
